slices.title: Manage versioned suites with separate measurement
slices.acceptance: Suites become versioned assets stored apart from the subjects they measure, with documentation, and changes to measurement go through their own approval so a subject can never change how it is measured. AC2: An agent-drafted suite change takes effect only through its own user-approved proposal, and a proposal that changes both a subject and a suite measuring it is refused. AC3: Only a person can accept an exception, and it records the check, matched instance, reason and approver.

slices.title: Compare revisions honestly and label evidence
slices.acceptance: Comparisons between revisions report declared methods, uncertainty and coverage, match settings except the subject under test, and produce evidence labels bound to exactly what was measured. AC1: A comparison reports each metric's declared method, uncertainty and minimum effect with counts, coverage and revision groups; a difference within uncertainty or below the minimum effect is inconclusive, and evidence below the suite's minimum sample or coverage is unvalidated. AC2: Both arms match every setting except the declared subject under test; production cohorts graded under different measurement revisions are regraded under one or reported non-comparable, and cohort differences and confounding changes are disclosed. AC3: Evidence is bound to immutable candidate, baseline and measurement identities, and a change to any of them returns it to unvalidated.

slices.title: Choose and pin DevWorks Auto once per new session
slices.acceptance: A1: New sessions selecting DevWorks Auto, including independently delegated worker sessions, classify from the initial prompt plus role/task context with an inspectable versioned rubric and accept only Low/Mid/High/Max. Native Home/sidebar and other route selectors, agent/host invocation and job route inputs use the same typed behavior. Explicit tier/named selections and upstream OpenRouter Auto/Auto Beta bypass classification, preserve independent effort/capabilities and keep provider-resolved identity distinct. Existing defaults and saved selections are not silently migrated. Latest aliases and available explicit versions use the same catalog across composers, host/agent and job inputs. A2: The initial tier and classifier/policy/input provenance survive concurrent first requests, availability waits and restart. Allocate/pin a generation member only within the chosen eligible tier. Later messages, tool turns, compaction, policy edits and complexity changes perform no further classification or tier switching; same-tier availability failover persists an explained replacement. Explicit manual overrides remain possible, established automatic assignment restoration does not reclassify, and a manually started session without an automatic assignment requires a new session for initial Auto routing. New/replacement generation allocations rotate latest-family/custom members; refreshing to a newer alias target leaves an eligible concrete version pin and its Auto tier unchanged, including across restart and first-request races. A3: SystemOne absence, unusable capabilities, malformed choices and bounded model failures lead to a directly admitted pinless Low classifier without recursive routing or conversation repinning. Low-model failures are bounded per model, and an exhausted/unsupported chosen generation tier waits or refuses rather than silently downgrading/upgrading. Classifier and generation usage/budget/authority are independently admitted and attributed. Deterministic native integration proves these paths and replay/cancellation behavior without inference in normal CI; reuse that evidence for final acceptance. The direct-Low fallback rotates latest Haiku/Luna plus configured custom Low members with its own purpose-scoped cursor and no conversation pin; missing models are excluded, returning models regain eligibility, and known replay neither retargets a decided alias nor advances a cursor.
slices.status: Approved plan; native implementation pending

slices.title: Keep latest model aliases and catalog availability current
slices.acceptance: AC1: Hourly/manual/overdue-on-reopen refreshes apply complete successful provider inventories per connection. Missing models remain stored with user settings/history intact and become unavailable; returning models regain availability without re-enabling user-disabled models. Failed, malformed or partial refreshes preserve the last successful inventory. Shared facts cover conversational/custom and SystemOne inventories; decision invocation/pool integration is owned by amended DW-22. AC2: All eight aliases resolve to the highest available parsed numeric family version within configured connection/policy scope, promote newly listed higher versions and fall back when a version disappears. New/replacement tier allocations round-robin latest-family targets and configured custom members. Eligible concrete pins survive promotion, turns and restart; explicit-version selection stays exact, known replay stays on its recorded resolution, and refresh/alias retargeting consumes no allocation turn. AC3: Every existing model-selection input, including Workspace/Home/sidebar and scheduled-job route inputs, offers latest aliases alongside available explicit versions. Unavailable records/configuration remain inspectable in Settings, selection/availability updates follow completed background/manual refreshes, and native UI and router/tool contracts share alias intent, resolved concrete identity and truthful unavailable states without bypassing effort, capabilities or provider constraints.
slices.status: Approved plan; native implementation pending
